correctness.rationale: After each line removal the only lost point pairs are the pairs on that removed line; distinct surviving line vertices are adjacent in the square exactly when nonparallel, and cross-shore adjacency is retained incidence by parity. Connectivity follows by joining points directly when possible, or via two nonparallel surviving lines and their intersection. Thus the point shore is the join of s q-point discrete factors with a nonempty simplex before the endpoint, and becomes a q-fold discrete join at s=q. The line shore has q full factors and one (q−s)-point factor until the latter is empty. Joins give the stated sphere counts and are simply connected for q≥3. The mixed simplices can have at most one vertex on one shore by four-cycle freeness. The two associated pieces collapse to the shores and intersect in the faulted incidence graph G_s. The graph is connected and its maps to both simply connected pieces are nullhomotopic, giving the actual wedge with ΣG_s; its cycle rank is b_s. For natural maps one uses Mayer–Vietoris, not the noncanonical wedge splitting. Deleting a line removes q incident edge coordinates; projecting graph cycles onto those coordinates has kernel exactly the smaller cycle lattice, with free quotient of rank q−1. In degree q the natural map before the endpoint is augmentation lattice inclusion tensored with the free top homology of the other q factors; projection to the missing augmentation coordinate gives a free quotient of rank (q−1)^q. Finally at q=3 the source shore classes have total rank 16 and map through vanishing H2 of the target shores; graph-cycle injectivity shows they are the full kernel, with image rank 10 and cokernel Z². For q≥4 neither final shore contributes H2. The closing line of Proof Step 5 uses source ambiguously at s=q−1, but both endpoint H_q groups are zero and the asserted map range is unambiguous.
residual_risks: Order-three binary checks match the four stage ranks and inclusion-image ranks; order-four checks are combinatorial only. No bundled code was executed, and the integral and arbitrary-plane conclusions follow from the independent structural argument, not the recorded calculations.

value.rationale: In a natural erasure of one affine direction the graph-cycle summand decreases uniformly, whereas a different homological degree appears at the last step. At order three those new classes sit in the same degree as the decreasing graph summand and constitute a rank-16 kernel despite primitive image. This is a useful integral boundary phenomenon and an all-stage map classification, not a re-evaluation of the endpoint Betti numbers.
residual_risks: Value is limited to one parallel class at inclusive scale two; no claim is made for arbitrary erasure patterns or for uniqueness in the literature.
